html:
The cravat is a neckscarf that spread through Europe from the 1630s, when Croatian mercenaries fighting for France in the Thirty Years' War wore knotted scarves around their necks.

The French called the style "à la croate", and the word cravate comes from the name of the Croats. It was taken up at the court of Louis XIV and in England after the Restoration, and over centuries it evolved into the modern necktie. Croatia marks 18 October as Cravat Day, and in 2003 an artist wrapped the arena of Pula in a giant red tie. The story shows how soldiers of the Habsburg border carried a small piece of Croatian dress into everyday life worldwide.
sum: The cravat is a neckscarf that spread through Europe from the 1630s, when Croatian mercenaries fighting for France in the Thirty Years' War wore knotted scarves around their necks.
